issue: Four one-line recall items are labeled analysis or evaluation with difficulty 3. That is two or more skill levels too high, and it inflates the module and section analysis/evaluation share that the Blueprint skill mix is measured against.
evidence: aud-ue-19 (analysis, d3): "Does this business risk always create a RMM?" The options are "Yes, every business risk does" / "Only if revenue falls this year" / "No, not necessarily" / "Only for public companies". This is recall of one principle, so remembering. aud-ue-24 (analysis, d3): "New ERP mid-year. How does this affect risk?" The options are "It lowers risk" / "No effect" / "It raises risk" / "Only IT staff are affected". Recall (the change factor), so remembering. aud-ue-26 (evaluation, d3): "What should the auditor evaluate?" The options are "A deficiency in that process" / "Nothing" / "Only the fee" / "Withdrawal". Recall of the AU-C 315 rule, so remembering/application. aud-ue-27 (evaluation, d3): "Control not in place. What follows?" The key "It isn't implemented" restates the stem, so application at most. Blueprint skill definitions: Analysis = examining the interrelationships of separate areas to identify causes and find evidence to support inferences. Evaluation = examining or assessing problems and using judgment to draw conclusions. None of these items requires either. Module label counts (practice + exam) are remembering 12, application 13, analysis 6, evaluation 2. After correction, the module has no genuine analysis or evaluation item.
source: AICPA Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints (2026), skill definitions; AUD skill allocation (Analysis 15-25%, Evaluation 5-15%)
fix: Relabel aud-ue-19 and aud-ue-24 to remembering, difficulty 1. Relabel aud-ue-26 to remembering (or application), difficulty 1-2. Relabel aud-ue-27 to application, difficulty 1-2. To keep the module's Area II analysis/evaluation coverage (AUD-II.B.1.3, II.E.4, II.E.5), write 2-3 real fact-pattern items. Example: a short client memo with several conditions. The learner picks which ones are FS-level vs assertion-level and the affected assertion, or evaluates whether a planned response addresses an assessed risk.

issue: Skill and difficulty are each one level too high. These scenario items need only applying a known link (customer distress -> receivable valuation; new product -> inventory valuation), and the three distractors are plainly irrelevant. Yet they are labeled analysis, difficulty 3.
evidence: aud-ue-09 distractors: existence of PP&E, completeness of accrued payroll, presentation of cash equivalents. aud-ue-14 distractors: completeness of cash receipts, existence of PP&E, classification of equity. aud-ue-25 distractors: "Only cash risks", "Only revenue risks", "No significant new risks". aud-ue-20 distractors: "Nothing, in a small entity", "A disclaimer of opinion", "Only the effect on audit fees". In each case one option is linked to the stem and the others are not, so these are application-level, difficulty 1-2.
fix: Relabel all four as application, difficulty 1 (aud-ue-25) or 2 (aud-ue-09, -14, -20). Or keep the analysis label and rewrite the distractors so they name other affected assertions. For aud-ue-09, for example: "completeness of revenue", "existence of receivables", "inventory valuation from lost volume". The learner must then reason which risk is most direct.

issue: The short-form items in the back half of the practice set use implausible distractors. Many also have the "only/nothing" absolute-word cue. A test-wise candidate can answer them without knowing the rule.
evidence: Examples. aud-ue-26: "Only the fee", "Withdrawal", "Nothing; the auditor found it". aud-ue-22: "Audit fees and billing terms", "Staff scheduling only". aud-ue-27: "Rely on the narrative", "Ignore the gap"; the key "It isn't implemented" restates the stem's "isn't actually in place". aud-ue-24: "Only IT staff are affected", "No effect". aud-ue-18: "Nothing; it's management's job". aud-ue-19: "Only for public companies"; the key is much the shortest. aud-ue-21 and aud-ue-23: all three distractors start or end with "only" and the key does not. aud-ue-17: b and c have "Only", d has "Nothing". aud-ue-25: a and b have "Only", c has "No significant"; the key "Going concern risk" is singular although the stem asks "Which risks rise?". cues.md flags absolutes confined to distractors in 11 of these 12 items.
source: Review brief section 2, per-MCQ check 6 (answer cues) and check 8 (realism)
fix: Rewrite the distractors as real misconceptions, with no absolute words. Examples. aud-ue-26: "Reassess control risk at maximum for all assertions" / "Communicate the risk to management only" / "Treat the risk as a significant risk automatically". aud-ue-23: "Operating effectiveness throughout the period" / "Whether the control was performed by an independent person" / "Whether management has documented the control". aud-ue-27: "Test the control's operating effectiveness with a larger sample" (keep). Reword the aud-ue-27 key to "Treat the control as not implemented and evaluate the deficiency".

issue: The choice explanations are circular, generic, or do not match their option, so a learner who picks a distractor is not told why it is wrong. One explanation answers a different option text.
evidence: aud-ue-16(c) "Only reading last year's report" is explained as "One visit is too limited." There is no visit in the option, so the explanation does not match it. aud-ue-16(d) says "Correct. AU-C 315." aud-ue-17(c) "Not sufficient." and (d) "More is required." aud-ue-18(c) "Not sufficient." aud-ue-19(b) "That isn't the test." and (d) "That isn't what the rule says." aud-ue-20(b) "Not automatically." aud-ue-22(b-d) "That is not the purpose." (x3). aud-ue-23(c,d) "Not the requirement." aud-ue-24(b) "It is relevant to risk." aud-ue-25(a,b) "More are affected." and (d) "Correct. Both are affected." ("both" has no referent). aud-ue-26(c) "That is not relevant." aud-ue-09(b-d), aud-ue-14(a,b) and aud-ue-15(a,b) all say "Not directly affected/indicated."
source: Review brief section 2, per-MCQ check 4 (explanations teach; not circular)
fix: Give each distractor one sentence naming the rule it breaks. Examples. aud-ue-16(c): "Reading the prior-year report is useful, but risk assessment procedures also require inquiry, analytical procedures, and observation/inspection (AU-C 315.14)." aud-ue-19(d): "AU-C 315 applies to all GAAS audits, not only issuers." aud-ue-25(d): "A declining industry plus high leverage raises going-concern, covenant-compliance and asset-impairment risks."

issue: aud-ue-16 and aud-ue-21 have the same stem ("Which procedures are risk assessment procedures?") and essentially the same key. The same list of risk assessment procedures is tested five times across modules, and aud-x2-39 is a near-copy of the aud-planning lesson check aud-pl-chk2.
evidence: cues.md Jaccard aud-ue-16 ~ aud-ue-21 = 1.00. The keys are "Inquiry, analytics and inspection" and "Inquiry and analytics". The skill labels disagree for the same item (application vs remembering). aud-x2-39 asks "Which procedure is not a risk assessment procedure?" with key "Confirming accounts receivable balances". aud-pl-chk2 (aud-planning) asks "Which is not a required risk assessment procedure?" with key "Confirmation of receivables". aud-x2-03 (aud-planning, on aud-mock-1 and -2) tests the same list again. aud-x2-39 is on aud-mock-3, so a learner meets on the mock an item they already answered as a lesson check.
source: Review brief section 2, per-MCQ check 7 (duplicates; same fact tested more than ~3 times)
fix: Delete aud-ue-21, or rewrite it as an application item: classify a described procedure, such as "reading industry trade journals during planning", as a risk assessment or a further procedure. Rewrite aud-x2-39 to test a different angle, such as the purpose of risk assessment procedures or the fact that they alone are not sufficient appropriate evidence for the opinion. Fix aud-ue-16's skill label to remembering.

issue: Exam item aud-x2-46 is a near-duplicate of aud-x2-04 (aud-planning), and both are on aud-mock-3. Four items test the one fact that the engagement team discussion covers susceptibility to misstatement, including fraud.
evidence: aud-x2-04: "Which statement about the engagement team discussion is correct?" Key: "It should cover how fraud could occur in the statements". aud-x2-46: "Which statement about the engagement team discussion required by AU-C 315 and AU-C 240 is correct?" Key: "It covers how fraud might occur in the statements". content/aud/exams/aud-mock-3.json lists both aud-x2-04 and aud-x2-46. The same fact is also tested by aud-ue-22 and aud-pl-06.
source: Review brief section 2, per-MCQ check 7; content/aud/exams/aud-mock-3.json
fix: Replace aud-x2-46 on aud-mock-3, or rewrite it to test another part of AU-C 315.17/240.15. Options: who must take part (key members, including the engagement partner); communicating matters to members not involved; setting aside beliefs about management's honesty and integrity. Retire aud-ue-22, or move it to aud-planning, where the discussion is taught.

issue: Exam item aud-x2-27 is the same question as lesson check aud-ue-chk1, with the same correct answer: control effectiveness is not an inherent risk factor. A learner who did the lesson recognizes it on aud-mock-2 instead of being assessed.
evidence: aud-ue-chk1: "Which is not one of the inherent risk factors in AU-C 315?" Key: "Effectiveness of internal control". aud-x2-27: "Which is not one of the inherent risk factors identified in SAS No. 145?" Key: "The effectiveness of the entity's controls". Distractors are Complexity/Change/Susceptibility vs Complexity/Subjectivity/Susceptibility. aud-x2-27 is on aud-mock-2.
fix: Rewrite aud-x2-27 as a scenario. For example: "An entity's pension obligation depends on a discount rate and mortality assumptions selected by management. Which inherent risk factors most directly apply?" The key is subjectivity and uncertainty; the distractors are change, complexity only, or control risk.

issue: Answer cues in two exam-pool items. In aud-x2-09 the key repeats the stem's keyword. In aud-x2-10 the key is much the longest option, and every distractor is narrowed by "one/single/specific", which signals assertion level.
evidence: aud-x2-09 asks which item is the factor "uncertainty"; the key is "An estimate that depends on uncertain future events". The key is also the longest option (51 characters vs 34-44). aud-x2-10 asks which risk is most likely at the FS level. The key is "Management that lacks financial reporting competence" (52 characters). The distractors are "Inventory valuation at one warehouse", "Existence of a single bank account" and "Cut-off of a specific revenue stream" (34-36 characters).
fix: aud-x2-09: change the key to "A warranty reserve based on expected future claims", which does not use the word "uncertain". aud-x2-10: make the distractors the same length and drop the narrowing words. For example: "Valuation of inventory held at third-party warehouses", "Completeness of accrued liabilities for a new benefit plan", "Cut-off of revenue under bill-and-hold arrangements". Shorten the key to "Management lacks accounting competence".

issue: Options (a) "Revenue will rise" and (c) "Revenue will rise 10%" overlap: (c) is a special case of (a). Both can be eliminated together, which leaves a two-way choice. The explanation also never shows the computation.
evidence: Recomputed: elasticity 2.0 x 5% price increase = about 10% drop in quantity. Revenue factor = 1.05 x 0.90 = 0.945, so revenue falls about 5.5%. Choice (c)'s +10% comes from treating the 10% quantity change as a revenue increase (wrong-sign label OK). The item-level explanation says only "Elastic demand (above 1): a price increase reduces total revenue."
source: Review brief section 2, per-MCQ checks 4 and 6
fix: Make the options mutually exclusive and numeric, and set calc: true. (a) Increase about 5% (ignores the quantity response). (b) No change (assumes unit elasticity). (c) Decrease 10% (confuses the quantity change with the revenue change). (d) Decrease about 5.5% (key). Add to the explanation: "%dQ = -2.0 x 5% = -10%; revenue = 1.05 x 0.90 = 0.945, about a 5.5% decline."

issue: Trap labels name computation errors on conceptual items that have no computation. "partial-computation" is used for under-inclusive "only X" distractors. "wrong-sign" is used for a conceptual reversal that aud-ue-03 labels "reversed".
evidence: partial-computation: aud-ue-chk2(a) "An assertion-level risk that affects revenue only"; aud-ue-10(c) "Only at the financial statement level"; aud-ue-16(c); aud-ue-17(b),(c); aud-ue-18(c); aud-ue-25(a),(b). wrong-sign: aud-ue-24(a) "It lowers risk". Every one of these items has calc = false.
source: src/content/schema.ts TRAP_TYPES; review brief check 2 (trap label matches misconception)
fix: Relabel as follows. aud-ue-chk2(a) and aud-ue-10(c): wrong-classification (risk level misclassified). aud-ue-16(c), aud-ue-17(b,c), aud-ue-18(c), aud-ue-25(a,b): wrong-rule (an incomplete statement of the requirement). aud-ue-24(a): reversed.

issue: The lesson, flashcard f5 and the explanation for aud-ue-05 attach "material items always get substantive procedures" to the SAS 145 stand-back. The stand-back (AU-C 315) only requires re-evaluating the determination. The substantive-procedure requirement is a separate AU-C 330 paragraph, and none of these places cites it. Its exact post-SAS 145 scope should be checked: material classes, or relevant assertions of significant classes.
evidence: lesson.md line 103: "Stand-back: for material items where no relevant assertion was identified, re-evaluate that conclusion. Material items always get substantive procedures." f5 back: "Re-evaluate material classes ... ; perform substantive procedures on all material items." aud-ue-05 explanation: "Stand-back requirement (SAS 145): ... Substantive procedures are required for every material class". The AU-C 315 stand-back (SAS 145) reads: for material classes of transactions, account balances or disclosures not determined to be significant, evaluate whether that determination remains appropriate. The substantive-procedures rule is AU-C 330.18. Pre-SAS 145 wording: "for all relevant assertions related to each material class". Two web searches did not confirm the SAS 145 amended wording; ISA 330.18 says "each material class". Other modules say "each material class" (aud-risk-response, aud-risk-materiality, aud-x2 item explanations, aud-tbs-u5-estimates), and aud-tbs-u5-estimates says "each relevant assertion of each material class". Each wording means something different when a material item has no relevant assertion.
source: AU-C 315 (as amended by SAS 145), stand-back paragraph; AU-C 330.18; ISA 330.18 (as conformed to ISA 315 (Revised 2019))
fix: Split the two rules in the lesson. (1) Stand-back (AU-C 315): re-evaluate the determination. (2) AU-C 330.18: substantive procedures regardless of assessed RMM, quoting the current wording. Do the same on f5, which then becomes two atomic cards, and in the aud-ue-05 explanation. Before publishing, check AU-C 330.18 as amended by SAS 145 and use one wording across all AUD modules.

issue: The lesson cites PCAOB AS 2110 but teaches only the AICPA (SAS 145) model. It never says that the PCAOB defines a significant risk differently, and that the PCAOB has no inherent risk spectrum and does not require separate inherent and control risk assessments. No AUD lesson teaches the PCAOB definition.
evidence: AS 2110 Appendix A defines a significant risk as "a risk of material misstatement that requires special audit consideration". AS 2110.70-.71 list factors to consider: fraud risk, recent significant developments, complexity, related-party transactions, subjectivity in measurement, and unusual transactions. A grep of content/ for "special audit consideration" returns nothing. The lesson's flashcard f2 and aud-ue-01 (the SAS 145 definition) are correctly labeled AICPA. Still, the lesson never warns that issuer audits use a different test, although the AUD exam covers both frameworks.
fix: Add a short "Issuer audits (PCAOB AS 2110)" note. It should give the PCAOB significant-risk definition ("requires special audit consideration") and the AS 2110.71 factors. It should also say that the inherent risk spectrum and the required separate IR/CR assessment are AICPA (SAS 145) concepts.

issue: Several items test content this lesson never teaches. Evaluating the design and implementation of controls, walkthroughs, and controls over significant risks are taught only in the next module (aud-internal-control). The auditor's evaluation of the entity's risk assessment process, and business risk vs RMM, are not taught in any AUD lesson.
evidence: lesson.md has no text on design and implementation, walkthroughs, controls over significant risks, the entity's risk assessment process, or business risks. A grep of the AUD lessons finds "walkthrough" and implementation only in aud-internal-control and aud-tests-of-controls, which come later in unit aud-u4/u5. "risk assessment process" appears only in aud-quality-management (the firm's process), and "business risk" appears in no lesson. Items affected: aud-ue-17 and aud-ue-23 (design and implementation), aud-ue-27 (walkthrough/implementation), aud-ue-20 and aud-ue-26 (the entity's risk assessment process), and aud-ue-19 (business risk vs RMM).
fix: Move aud-ue-17, -23 and -27 to aud-internal-control. Add a short section to this lesson covering three points. (a) Business risks vs RMM: not every business risk leads to an RMM. (b) The entity's risk assessment process: understand it, judge whether it suits the entity's nature and complexity, and if a risk was missed, ask why. (c) For significant risks, identify the controls that address them and evaluate their design and implementation. Alternatively, retire aud-ue-19, -20 and -26.

issue: Both items use the pre-SAS 145 wording "evaluate whether the absence ... is a significant deficiency or material weakness" for the entity's risk assessment process. They leave out SAS 145's scalability test: whether the process is appropriate to the entity's nature and complexity. For a small entity, an informal, undocumented process can be appropriate.
evidence: aud-ue-20 stem: "A small client has no formal process for identifying business risks." Key: "A possible significant deficiency". Explanation: "The absence of an appropriate risk assessment process may be a significant deficiency or material weakness." aud-ue-26 explanation: "If management's process failed to identify a material risk, the auditor considers whether a significant deficiency exists." Under AU-C 315 as amended by SAS 145, the auditor evaluates whether the entity's risk assessment process is appropriate to its circumstances given its nature and complexity. When the auditor finds an RMM that management missed, the auditor first decides whether it is a risk of a kind the process should have found, then why it failed, and only then whether a control deficiency exists. The keys are still the best options offered.
source: AU-C 315 (as amended by SAS 145), requirements on the entity's risk assessment process and the identification of control deficiencies
fix: aud-ue-20: change the key to "Whether an informal process is appropriate given the entity's nature and complexity, and whether a control deficiency exists". Add to the explanation that informal processes are common and can be appropriate in less complex entities. aud-ue-26: rewrite the explanation in the SAS 145 order: is it a risk the process should have identified, why did it fail, is the process appropriate, then is there a deficiency.

issue: Pure economics content may be outside the AUD Blueprint and is not marked optional. This covers supply and demand, the elasticity calculation, MR = MC profit maximization, and classifying leading, coincident and lagging indicators. Under CPA Evolution, BEC economic concepts moved to the BAR discipline, which this platform does not offer. AUD-II.B.1 covers understanding economic conditions as an external factor that affects RMM, not microeconomics.
evidence: lesson.md "Economic conditions" section and objective 4 (which has no task reference). aud-ue-11 tests the revenue effect of elasticity; aud-ue-12 tests indicator classification. AUD-II.B.1.1 in review/reference/blueprint-tasks.csv reads "Identify external factors (industry, regulatory, economic and the applicable financial reporting framework)" (reconstructed). One web search found a secondary source saying economics, internal control and IT concepts moved from BEC into BAR and ISC; it did not confirm the 2026 AUD task text. REVIEW.md P1-7 added this content deliberately, so it is a prior decision to confirm.
source: AICPA 2026 AUD and BAR Blueprints (not fetched); https://open-exam-prep.com/study-guides/cpa/exam-structure-licensure/cpa-evolution-model (secondary)
fix: Check the 2026 AUD Blueprint Area II.B task text. If it does not list these economics concepts, mark aud-ue-11 and aud-ue-12 optional and move the microeconomics into an optional sidebar. Keep the audit application ("a contracting, price-elastic market raises inventory valuation and credit-loss risk") and test that instead. For example: "Demand for the client's product is elastic and a competitor cut prices 10%. Which assertion is most at risk?"

issue: The SOX table says §404(b) auditor attestation applies to "accelerated and large accelerated filers" without the emerging growth company exemption. A learner would wrongly conclude that an EGC which is an accelerated filer needs an ICFR audit.
evidence: lesson.md line 121: "§404(b) | The auditor attests to ICFR (accelerated and large accelerated filers)". JOBS Act §103 exempts EGCs from §404(b) whatever their filer status. Non-accelerated filers are exempt under Dodd-Frank §989G.
fix: Change the row to: "The auditor attests to ICFR for accelerated and large accelerated filers. Non-accelerated filers and emerging growth companies are exempt."

issue: The elasticity rule is stated without absolute value. Price elasticity of demand computed as %dQ / %dP is negative, so "greater than 1" and "less than 1" should refer to the absolute value.
evidence: lesson.md line 108: "Price elasticity of demand = % change in quantity / % change in price. Elastic (greater than 1) ... Inelastic (less than 1)". aud-ue-11 gives the elasticity as +2.0, which is consistent only with the absolute-value convention.
fix: Write: "Elastic (|E| > 1) ... Inelastic (|E| < 1); elasticity is usually quoted as an absolute value."

issue: The big-idea example maps the allocation and standalone-price judgments in a bundled subscription arrangement to revenue "occurrence and cut-off". Allocation complexity and standalone-selling-price subjectivity mainly affect accuracy/valuation of the amounts recognized, plus cut-off and timing.
evidence: bigIdea.example: "Revenue now involves complexity (allocation), subjectivity (standalone prices), and change (a new model), so revenue occurrence and cut-off move toward the high end of the inherent risk spectrum."
source: AU-C 315 (SAS 145) inherent risk factors; ASC 606 allocation
fix: Change "occurrence and cut-off" to "accuracy (allocation) and cut-off (timing over the subscription term)".
